    Dune Meadows: Planned Contrasts and Pairwise Comparisons

    dune-contrasts-posthoc.Rmd

    An omnibus management effect says whether some meadow-community centroids differ. Phase 13 asks narrower questions after the factor and contrast family have been chosen. This vignette uses the four-level Management factor and Bray–Curtis dissimilarities.

    management_data <- data.frame(
  Management = droplevels(dune.env$Management)
)
management_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ Management,
  management_data,
  vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
)
table(management_data$Management)
#> 
#> BF HF NM SF 
#>  3  5  6  6

    Planned contrasts

    A contrast is a coefficient vector applied to the unweighted group centroids. Its coefficients must sum to zero. Here the first contrast compares BF with HF; the second compares their average with the average of NM and SF.

    planned <- rbind(
  `BF - HF` = c(BF = 1, HF = -1, NM = 0, SF = 0),
  `managed pair - other pair` = c(BF = 0.5, HF = 0.5, NM = -0.5, SF = -0.5)
)

planned_fit <- permanova_contrasts(
  management_design,
  contrasts = planned,
  adjust = "holm",
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260719
)
planned_fit
#> One-factor distance contrasts
#> Family: user-specified one-factor centroid contrasts 
#> Multiplicity adjustment: holm 
#>                   contrast df        ss        ms denominator_df  pseudo_f
#>                    BF - HF  1 0.1617135 0.1617135             16 0.9141421
#>  managed pair - other pair  1 0.5627522 0.5627522             16 3.1811546
#>  p_perm p_adjusted adjustment
#>    0.46       0.46       holm
#>    0.03       0.06       holm

    Each test retains every group-centroid direction orthogonal to the requested contrast as nuisance structure. Its Freedman–Lane residual permutation is therefore contrast specific. Holm adjustment controls the family without requiring the two planned contrasts to be orthogonal.

    All pairwise differences

    permanova_pairwise() constructs the six pairwise coefficient rows and uses the same contrast engine. The default Holm adjustment is appropriate under arbitrary dependence among overlapping pairs.

    pairwise_fit <- permanova_pairwise(
  management_design,
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260719
)
pairwise_fit
#> One-factor distance contrasts
#> Family: all pairwise one-factor centroid differences 
#> Multiplicity adjustment: holm 
#>  contrast df        ss        ms denominator_df  pseudo_f p_perm p_adjusted
#>   BF - HF  1 0.1617135 0.1617135             16 0.9141421  0.460       0.46
#>   BF - NM  1 0.5662456 0.5662456             16 3.2009023  0.025       0.10
#>   BF - SF  1 0.4016624 0.4016624             16 2.2705377  0.070       0.21
#>   HF - NM  1 0.6513088 0.6513088             16 3.6817517  0.010       0.05
#>   HF - SF  1 0.2828804 0.2828804             16 1.5990807  0.175       0.35
#>   NM - SF  1 0.7575728 0.7575728             16 4.2824464  0.005       0.03
#>  adjustment
#>        holm
#>        holm
#>        holm
#>        holm
#>        holm
#>        holm

    The raw and adjusted p-values answer different questions. p_perm is the contrast-specific empirical p-value; p_adjusted accounts for the full family shown in the result. These are location contrasts, so a separate dispersion analysis remains advisable when ecological spread differences are plausible.

    Phase 13 intentionally stops at one fixed factor. Contrasts in multifactor or mixed models require an explicit marginal-mean weighting rule and a design-specific denominator; they are not inferred from this one-factor API.
